title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 33-35): p.33 is a 'formulaire' for SL(2,Z) and GL(2,Z), described as the oriented and full Teichmüller modular groups of type (0,3) and (1,1). It uses rho (order 6 in SL(2,Z), order 3 mod +-1), the order-4 elements sigma_i, the unipotents epsilon_i = 1+N_i, l_i = epsilon_i^2, lambda_i = -l_i with lambda_inf lambda_1 lambda_0 = 1, and the reflections tau_i, tau'_i. p.35 (June 1983) restarts axiomatically from a group H generated by epsilon_0, epsilon_1 with the braid relation epsilon_0 epsilon_1 epsilon_0 = epsilon_1 epsilon_0 epsilon_1. That group is B_3, the central extension of SL(2,Z).

This page computes in a group where the relations of the formulaire are 'twisted' by an element phi, and sigma_inf(phi) denotes the conjugate of phi by sigma_inf. On p.35 conjugation by sigma exchanges epsilon_0 and epsilon_1, so sigma_inf(phi) is plausibly phi(y,x) when phi = phi(x,y). The page states three things:
(1) [l_0,l_1] = [lambda_0,lambda_1] = X^3, where X := sigma_inf(phi) rho^{-1} = l_0 rho = rho l_inf. The commutators agree because the signs are central.
(2) [sigma_inf,l_inf] = [sigma_inf,lambda_inf] = (sigma_inf(phi^{-1}) rho)^3. Writing g = sigma_inf(phi^{-1}), one has g rho = g (rho g) g^{-1}, so this cube is a conjugate of [l_0,l_1] (or of its inverse, depending on the commutator convention).
(3) Hence [lambda_0,lambda_1] = 1 <=> [sigma_inf,l_inf] = 1 <=> (sigma_inf(phi) rho^{-1})^3 = 1.

The purpose is to translate a commutation condition between 'Dehn twists' l_0, l_1 (and between sigma_inf and l_inf) into a cube or order-3 relation on 'phi times rotation'. This is exactly the shape of the 'hexagon' relation for an element (lambda, f) acting on the profinite completion of B_3 or pi_1(P^1-{0,1,inf}). Drinfeld's relation f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m f(x,y)x^m = 1 can be rewritten as (f.rho)^3 = 1 using the cyclic symmetry rho of order 3. The page therefore looks like a step in Grothendieck's 1981-83 derivation of the defining relations of what became the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group: equivalent forms of the 'level (0,3)/(1,1)' Lego relation. It does not hold with phi = 1 in SL(2,Z) itself. There l_0 rho = [[2,-1],[-1,1]] is hyperbolic, and l_0, l_1 generate a free group. So phi must be a genuine twisting element, or the identities are meant in a different (completed or quotient) group.
errors: (sigma_inf(phi^{-1}) rho)^3 is conjugate to (rho sigma_inf(phi^{-1}))^3 = X^{-3} = [l_0,l_1]^{-1}, not to [l_0,l_1] itself, unless the commutator convention compensates. The stated 'int(sigma)(phi^{-1}).[l_0,l_1]' is therefore correct only up to inversion and convention. The equivalences in line 3 are unaffected.
The conjugating element is written int(sigma)(phi^{-1}). It should presumably be int(sigma_inf(phi^{-1})), i.e. conjugation by sigma_inf(phi^{-1}); the notation is ambiguous.
The identities cannot hold in SL(2,Z) with phi = 1 (l_0 rho has trace 3). The ambient group and the meaning of phi are not specified on the page.

ideas.what: Rewriting a commutation condition between twists ([l_0,l_1] = 1, equivalently [sigma_inf,l_inf] = 1) as an order-3 relation (sigma_inf(phi) rho^{-1})^3 = 1 involving a twisting element phi and the order-3 rotation rho
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon (order-3 / cyclic) relation for elements (lambda,f) of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group; (f rho)^3 = 1 form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990); Ihara (1990-91) for the Galois-side formulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the 'Lego' principle that the tower is determined by levels <= 2 with relations from (0,3),(1,1),(0,4),(0,5); no explicit formula of this kind is published

ideas.what: Conjugacy of the two cubes and of the two commutators

missed.claim: Explicit 1981-83 manuscript computation, by Grothendieck, of the order-3 (hexagon-type) relation (sigma_inf(phi) rho^{-1})^3 = 1. It is shown equivalent to the commutation of twists in the modular group of type (1,1)/(0,3). This predates Drinfeld's and Ihara's published formulations of GT.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the concrete defining relations of GT-like objects in hand, not just the Lego philosophy. That is of historical interest for crediting; the mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a short, partly convention-dependent computation. Its interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck working out what amounts to the order-3/hexagon relation of the GT group in explicit form years before Drinfeld. His priority for the general idea, however, is already known through the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: Above '=1' in the third line, after [σ∞,ℓ∞], Grothendieck has written '[λ0,λ1]' as an annotation. It is not part of the equality chain.
'int(σ)(φ^{-1})' is likely meant as int(σ∞(φ^{-1})); the subscript ∞ is barely visible.
The '‖' below [λ0,λ1] in line 3 is an unfinished equality sign, linking it vertically to [ℓ0,ℓ1].
